problem: What is the value of $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡(3x+\frac{\pi }{4})+2$ at its local maximum points?

feedback.problem: What is the value of $f(x)=-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})+3$ at its local minimum points?
feedback.worked_solution:
On a negative branch of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x\le -1.
$$

The points where $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=-1$ are **local maximums** of the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$ For now, we're interested in the local maximums (not local minimums) of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ because we see that $f(x)$ contains a vertical reflection.

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})\le -1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-\frac{2}{3}$ and adding $3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})\le -1 \\  & -\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})\ge \frac{2}{3} \\  & -\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})+3\ge \frac{2}{3}+3 \\  & -\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})+3\ge \frac{11}{3} \\  & f(x)\ge \frac{11}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\frac{11}{3}$ at its local minimum points.
